coverage_claim: Source-grounded Vercy reviewable-draft specification of Product Configuration / Variant aggregate with 12 finding records, 7 functions, 48 questions and 9 qualified sources. Coverage includes identity, lifecycle, relationships, temporal, provenance, ownership, validation, access, interoperability, properties and retention dimensions. Operational implementation, real solver fixtures, executable instance schema, sector-specific profiles and licensed ISO clause inspection remain deferred. No external Claude or Grok research was admitted; single-provider result requires separate no-tools audit and publication hold visible in all artifacts.

boundary_decision.rationale: WM-OBJ-017 owns a bounded, versioned configuration definition with internal consistency rules, lifecycle state (partial/resolved/released/superseded), and composition layers (identity, selections, evaluation, properties, baseline, governance). The frozen registry record classifies this as 'standalone-mm' packaging kind, distinct from entry_kind schema. The structure demonstrates aggregate characteristics: owns a coherent root, carries resolved state transitions, enforces internal constraints (release gate, completeness checks, constraint evaluation), and delegates external masters (family, design, BOM, offer). Entry kind of 'entity' would flatten internal hierarchy; 'relationship' would misplace mastership responsibility. Aggregate is defensible and consistent with the declared scope.

decisions.rationale: Frozen relationship contract explicitly permits REFERENCE with 'classifies' semantics because the research schema enum lacks CLASSIFIES. The six boundary-note findings correctly identify this as a deliberate substitution, not a schema failure. Instance items are separate aggregates; this variant merely qualifies their class and interpretation. The mapping is documented and reversible.

The service-layer guidance correctly names six roles (owner, steward, author, reviewer, release authority, projection maintainer) and declares access scopes (bundle/layer/finding/artifact). AGENTS.md bootstrap field list exists. However, this specification defines the *information contract* and governance *rules*, not a live Dimension instance. Actual instantiation—who holds each role, which Dimension registry, access token scopes—remains external. Acceptance records that the model correctly positions this as a service-layer responsibility, not a self-contained runtime.

Nine sources cited: Schema.org (vocabulary, authority tier 2), GS1 GDSN CPV guideline (tier 1), Microsoft Dynamics 365 (tier 2), OASIS UBL (tier 1), W3C PROV-DM (tier 1), IETF RFC 3339 (tier 1), ISO 10007 and 10303-242 (tier 1, public abstracts only). Vocabulary and guideline sources are fully inspected. Licensed ISO standards are inspected through public scope abstracts only, not normative clauses. This is appropriate for a proposed information contract; full ISO conformance verification is explicitly deferred. Known omission is transparent.

decisions.disposition: accepted as proposed Vercy extension with evidence requirement
decisions.rationale: The specification treats 'qualified direct properties' and 'capability envelope' as proposed Vercy extensions beyond product-family and engineering-design scopes. The coverage checklist explicitly records this as a proposed design choice, not a universal requirement. Every property (mass, hardness, dimension, load limit) is marked as requiring independent evidence and units. No fabricated observations are claimed. The four questions per layer (classification, measurement, quality, evidence) correctly enforce that properties remain unknown unless supplied. Acceptance records the proposal; implementation requires sector-specific evidence fixtures and owner approval.

decisions.concept: Claude and Grok waiver visibility in publication
decisions.rationale: The evidence pack documents that Claude timed out after three bounded attempts (1800s, 900s, 600s/300s) and Grok is waived for completion. The provider policy explicitly permits Codex to complete source-grounded fallback work. However, the publication holds must expose this in every artifact: not merely 'reviewable-draft,' but explicitly 'independent Claude and Grok review is waived by repository-owner authorization dated 2026-09-06.' Absence of external review is a material fact for any downstream consumer. Acceptance requires that every published version (schema, documentation, model registry entry) carry a clear hold and waiver statement.

WM-OBJ-018 (Engineering Design) and WM-OBJ-019 (BOM) remain external masters. This variant references selected revisions and applicability, never owns them. The specification correctly refuses to manage design lifecycle, solver implementation, or component-level quantities. Boundary-note findings correctly distinguish: variant selects revisions, engineering masters retain independent authority. The design-effectivity layer correctly asks 'which BOM *selected*' not 'which BOM owned.' Acceptance records that composition mastery is correctly preserved and not collapsed into this aggregate.

publication_holds: Live URL verification required: All nine source URLs (Schema.org, GS1, Microsoft Learn, OASIS, W3C, IETF, ISO) must be confirmed accessible and at stated versions before publication. Inspect SRC-004 Microsoft Learn page updated 2026-05-06 for any breaking changes between 2026-05-06 and publication date.

Owner-authorized single-provider waiver must be visible in all artifacts: Every published form (JSON, schema documentation, model registry entry, AGENTS.md reference) shall carry an explicit hold statement: 'Independent Claude and Grok review is waived by repository-owner authorization dated 2026-09-06. Codex result admits no external provider validation. Reviewable-draft status pending optional supplemental audit or explicit publication release.'

Dimension instantiation and AGENTS.md bootstrap must precede live service-layer deployment: The specification defines governance roles and access scopes but does not instantiate a live Dimension, registry, or access-control system. No variant instance may be created or released until the owning Dimension declares its steward, release authority, and access policy in accordance with the named roles.

ISO clause inspection must be completed for full normative conformance claim: The specification inspects ISO 10007 (configuration management) and ISO 10303-242 (STEP model-based 3D) only through public abstracts. If any instance is claimed to conform to these standards normatively, licensed clause inspection and reconciliation are required. Until then, conformance claims remain limited to vocabulary (Schema.org, GS1, OASIS, W3C, IETF, Microsoft) sources.

Sector-specific profiles and physical-property evidence fixtures must be supplied before certification use: The proposed physical-signature and capability-envelope findings explicitly note that automotive, medical, food, aerospace, building-product and regulated-market sectors require specialist evidence, unit conventions and fixtures. No instance may be certified as meeting a sector standard without that profile instantiation.
deferred_research: Solver adapter implementation conformance: The evaluate-configuration function correctly refuses to implement a solver and instead invokes 'a separately approved bounded evaluator' whose result is retained. No executable constraint-satisfaction, linear programming or SAT solver is supplied. Sector adoption requires binding to real solvers (Z3, Gurobi, CPLEX) and integration fixtures; this remains on hold pending solver-agnostic evaluation receipt schema.

Round-trip projection fixtures for Schema.org, GS1 GDSN and OASIS UBL: The projection-loss findings define the loss-report structure and questions but supply no actual bidirectional conversion code or test fixtures. Adoption requires demonstrating that variant identity, selections, rules and provenance survive round-trip through at least Schema.org ProductModel and GS1 CPV profiles without silent data loss. Test vectors are deferred.

Regulated-context and compliance-specific evidence templates: The mastership-disclosure layer correctly identifies that confidential design and customer selections require scoped access control. No actual implementation of time-limited disclosure, redaction templates, audit-log schema or retention schedules is supplied. Regulated sectors (medical device, pharmaceutical, food safety) require compliance-specific evidence and field-level retention policies before deployment.

Physical properties and measurement evidence schema: The capability-envelope layer correctly requires independent evidence for every physical claim. No schema for unit conversion, uncertainty quantification, test conditions, material specifications or measurement traceability is provided. Adoption requires working with sector metrology and product-safety standards (IEC, ASTM, ISO VIM) to ground physical properties in measurable evidence.

Live Dimension registry and instance-creation fixtures: The service-layer bootstrap names AGENTS.md and declares required fields but does not supply a working registry, instance-creation workflow or access-token binding. Adoption requires implementing the Dimension registry endpoint, namespace allocation, revision pinning, digest verification and audit-log capture described in the artifact rules.
